<mxCell id="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-30" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;"><font style="font-size: 15px;">Receive Synchronization from a Listener Perspective</font></h1><div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">Using SonoBusMendeni, when the Sync Receive button is pushed&nbsp; &nbsp;a. all streams from remote players are synchronized by measuring the receive latency from each, noting the largest value and then padding the receive jitter buffer. The calculation is:</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">deltaMs = maxrecvMs - currentRecvMs</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">newPeerBuffer = currentPeerBuffer + deltaMs</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">Where maxrecvMs is the largest receive latency in the set of remote peers. An extra 2ms of padding is added to improve&nbsp; overall listening experience by preventing drops that might be on the ragged edge.</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">In our example session, 55ms is the largest receive latency (Pink player) from the three Remote Musicians. Adding 2ms for extra padding, the value is 57ms.</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">Let's say the Orange player has a current jitter buffer value of 8ms:</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">45 = 57 - 12</font></div><div><span style="font-size: 14px;">53 =&nbsp; 8 + 45</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 14px;"><br></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 14px;">The new jitter buffer value is set to 53ms. This is all done on the listener side - players are unaware as nothing ever changes from their perspective.</span></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">The result is close to a perfect listening experience regardless of where the audience is located. Successful synchronization is highly dependent on stable connections for all players and the listener.</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">The receive sync process is idempotent, meaning the button can be pushed (forcing a recalibration of maxrecvMs) when new players arrive/leave or network conditions change. Resetting in the middle of a song is not recommended as recallibration can be audible.</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">Local Musicians can also participate by using headphones for a traditional SonoBus session experience (shown) or play along to the synchronized House PA (not show). Playing with the PA will increase overall latency to the other remote players, but they can turn down the venue musician(s) to reduce distraction.</font></div></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="808" width="400" x="434" y="32" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-31" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" value="SonoBus "Player"" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="57" width="129" x="263" y="425" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-32" edge="1" parent="1" source="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-31" style="endArrow=classic;startArrow=none;html=1;rounded=0;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;strokeColor=light-dark(#000000,#3399FF);strokeWidth=2;entryX=0.682;entryY=-0.1;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;entryPerimeter=0;startFill=0;" target="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-29" value=""> <mxGeometry height="50" relative="1" width="50" as="geometry"> <Array as="points" /> <mxPoint x="330" y="360" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="378" y="549" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="MMU7wC4jm6lLepNU2r36-33" parent="1" style="shape=image;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;labelBackgroundColor=default;verticalAlign=top;aspect=fixed;imageAspect=0;editableCssRules=.*;image=data:image/svg+xml,;" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="18.45" width="17" x="500" y="99.55000000000001" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="wqusKDDBDGM86phBFI-r-1" parent="1" style="shape=image;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;labelBackgroundColor=default;verticalAlign=top;aspect=fixed;imageAspect=0;editableCssRules=.*;image=data:image/svg+xml,;" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="47.8" width="44.03" x="120" y="299.2" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

h1.font: Receive Synchronization from a Listener Perspective

div.font: Using SonoBusMendeni, when the Sync Receive button is pushed a. all streams from remote players are synchronized by measuring the receive latency from each, noting the largest value and then padding the receive jitter buffer. The calculation is:

Where maxrecvMs is the largest receive latency in the set of remote peers. An extra 2ms of padding is added to improve overall listening experience by preventing drops that might be on the ragged edge.
In our example session, 55ms is the largest receive latency (Pink player) from the three Remote Musicians. Adding 2ms for extra padding, the value is 57ms.
Let's say the Orange player has a current jitter buffer value of 8ms:

div.span: The new jitter buffer value is set to 53ms. This is all done on the listener side - players are unaware as nothing ever changes from their perspective.

div.font: The result is close to a perfect listening experience regardless of where the audience is located. Successful synchronization is highly dependent on stable connections for all players and the listener.

The receive sync process is idempotent, meaning the button can be pushed (forcing a recalibration of maxrecvMs) when new players arrive/leave or network conditions change. Resetting in the middle of a song is not recommended as recallibration can be audible.

Local Musicians can also participate by using headphones for a traditional SonoBus session experience (shown) or play along to the synchronized House PA (not show). Playing with the PA will increase overall latency to the other remote players, but they can turn down the venue musician(s) to reduce distraction.
